old_caption: The video captures a serene scene of a misty river bordered by dense green forest. The water is calm, reflecting the surrounding trees and creating a tranquil atmosphere. A long log lies horizontally across the river, partially submerged, adding a natural element to the landscape. The forest on the opposite bank remains static, providing a lush backdrop to the misty river. The overall mood of the video is one of quiet beauty and natural serenity.
original_wisa_caption: The video captures a serene scene of a misty river bordered by dense green forest. The water is calm, reflecting the surrounding trees and creating a tranquil atmosphere. A long log lies horizontally across the river, partially submerged, adding a natural element to the landscape. As the video progresses, a light mist rises from the water's surface, drifting slowly across the river, enhancing the peaceful ambiance. The mist appears to be moving gently from left to right, suggesting a slight breeze. The forest on the opposite bank remains static, providing a lush backdrop to the misty river. The overall mood of the video is one of quiet beauty and natural serenity, with no visible movement or activity other than the subtle movement of the mist.
caption: The video captures a moving view across calm, rippled water, bordered by a steep, forested cliff and a low mist band hovering at its base. In the foreground a log boom of long floating logs runs diagonally across the lower scene, carrying several small perched birds and a yellow-green marker near its middle. Over time the foreground arrangement, mist band, and cliff drift toward the left while the viewpoint continuously translates. The boom's diagonal angle flattens slightly as the viewpoint shifts, consistent with parallax. The birds stay on the logs, making only minor posture adjustments. The mist subtly thickens and shifts shape near the cliff base, while the water shows small ripples. New portions of the boom and cliff enter from the right as existing foreground elements move leftward.

endpoints are normal, not physical errors. Do not add unseen causes, onset, stopping or outcomes.
An internal editing cut is not evidence of physical motion connecting the views.

Check identification before physical interpretation: a reflection is not a separate actor;
a powder/smoke/liquid outline or shadow is not automatically the boundary of a solid object;
an apparent change caused by occlusion/viewpoint is not automatically material deformation.
Do not claim contact, bending, compression, melting, disintegration or structural recovery unless
the appropriate material/surface itself provides visible evidence. Do not infer a force or earlier
collision just because the visible configuration would be compatible with it.

camera tracking. A single visible texture/seam does not prove spin. Avoid unnecessary absolute
claims of stillness, no motion, no camera motion or 'exactly' synchronized changes.
Remove invented scene details and explanations, but keep clearly visible ongoing motion and
processes. Avoid deleting the real process merely because its cause lies outside the cropped window.
